description: Two ways, picked by what is available. WITH a connection string (this server's KN_DATABASE_URL environment variable): copies the SHAPE of the Postgres/Supabase database (never its rows) into a throwaway schema, attacks the copy - can a stranger read or change data, can one customer read another's, can the same thing exist twice - reports in plain English, and deletes the copy; 2-3 minutes. WITHOUT one: pass app_url, the running app's web address, and it reads the app the way a stranger's browser does and reports which tables anyone on the internet can read - counts only, nothing written, about 10 seconds. NEVER ask the person to paste a connection string into the chat. Long runs return a job to follow with kryptheon_job.

app_url.description: The running app's web address, e.g. https://my-app.example.com - used when no connection string is configured. Never a database connection string.

schema.description: The schema the app lives in. Leave it out: it is "public" for almost everyone.

name: kryptheon_scan_database
title: Attack a copy of the database
